chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

he was asked about a man who shot at prey while he was upon a mountain or a wall, and the arrow pierced into it and it died. So he said: Eat from it. But if it fell into the water from your shooting and it died, then do not eat from it.

key_terms.حائط: A wall — here indicating elevated ground used as a hunting platform
key_terms.رمية: A single shot or throw — the act of launching a projectile

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating prey that fell into water after being shot with an arrow?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about the permissibility of hunting prey shot from an elevated position (mountain or wall). He ruled that the meat is permissible if the arrow was the direct cause of death, but if the prey fell into water and died there, the water becomes an uncertain cause of death, rendering the meat impermissible. This ruling reflects the Islamic principle that certainty of the lawful cause of slaughter is required for permissibility.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about a man who shot as a prey, and he was upon a mountain, or a wall, so the arrow pierced into it, so it died’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat from it, and if it falls into the water from it being shot, so it dies, so do not eat from it’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a man who shoots a prey on a mountain or wall.

The arrow pierces into it and it dies. He (the Imam) said, ‘You can use it for food; but if it falls in water and dies, then do not eat it. 5 ” Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy from ‘Abd Allah ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated a similar Hadith. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from certain persons of our people from Hisham ibn Salim from Sama‘ah from ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated a similar Hadith.
